name: CHROMEWORKS Silhouette Precision Pro Arm
description:
The Silhouette Precision Pro is Chromeworks' flagship surgical and fine-motor arm, engineered around a brushed-titanium chassis with 24 individually actuated micro-servo finger segments capable of sub-0.1mm positional accuracy. The neural feedback mesh runs at 2ms latency and includes a tremor-cancellation algorithm that actively counteracts organic nervous system noise, producing a hand steadier than any unaugmented human. A haptic skin layer over the fingertips replicates pressure and texture feedback with clinical fidelity, making it indistinguishable from organic touch in most tasks.

The Silhouette Pro is the standard of care among tier 3-5 surgeons, master watchmakers, demolitions technicians, and high-precision fabricators throughout the Great Lakes megacity. Chromeworks markets it aggressively to medical institutions, and its sleek mirrored-chrome aesthetic has become shorthand for professional excellence — seeing one on a surgeon's arm in a Spire hospital inspires immediate confidence. In lower tiers, bootleg firmware unlocks exist that push the tremor-cancellation beyond safe thresholds, used by forgers and micro-electronics thieves.
installation_requirements: Full shoulder disarticulation, Chromeworks-certified neural integration surgeon, proprietary neural mapping session pre-op
rejection_risk: Low — biocompatible polymer interface layer and Chromeworks' proprietary NeuroSync bonding protocol minimize rejection
maintenance: Bi-annual servo calibration, haptic skin layer replacement every 18 months, firmware update subscription required

side_effects: Sensory uncanny valley effect — haptic feedback occasionally misreads temperature gradients, causing mild disorientation
Neural feedback mesh can cause hypersensitivity to vibration, making loud industrial environments uncomfortable
Proprietary firmware lock-in means unauthorized modifications trigger warranty void and remote diagnostic flags
Extended fine-motor tasking without rest periods causes phantom fatigue signals in the shoulder socket
cultural_context: In the Spire tiers, a Chromeworks Silhouette on a surgeon or craftsperson is a credential as much as a limb — clients specifically request practitioners who wear them. The mirrored chrome finish has become so associated with elite precision work that knockoff cosmetic sleeves mimicking the look are sold in tier 2 markets.
known_users: High-end forgers and counterfeiters (grey market firmware)
story_hooks: A renowned surgeon's Silhouette Pro is remotely bricked mid-operation via a firmware exploit — someone wanted the patient to die on the table
Underground tremor-cancellation firmware is being sold that allows pickpockets to lift items with zero perceptible movement — traced back to a disgruntled Chromeworks engineer
A demolitions tech with a Silhouette Pro is the only person who can disarm a device — but their arm's maintenance subscription has lapsed and calibration is drifting
